title: SLO targets and rollout gates for Hosted API production rollout
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description: Define measurable SLOs (latency, availability, error budget) for the Hosted API vNext rollout and codify rollout gates and automatic rollback thresholds. This ticket captures target numbers, monitoring/alerting configuration, burn-rate policies, and acceptance criteria needed for the PM sign-off prior to progressive exposure beyond internal beta.
background: We are preparing to roll out the updated serving runtime and model routing changes to Hosted API customers. Previous incidents highlighted tail-latency regressions under bursty load and a lack of clear automated rollback thresholds. This work aligns SLOs with customer expectations, ties error budgets to rollout cadence, and ensures Console dashboards + alerts surface regressions within minutes.
scope: In-scope: SLO target values (p50/p95/p99), uptime SLA baseline, error budget burn-rate rules, monitoring/alerting queries, canary/capacity gate definitions, visibility in Console. Out-of-scope: pricing changes, Dedicated/Private-specific SLOs (will be separate tickets).
slo_definitions: 1) Latency: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 400ms for text-generation token append operations at typical seq_len=128 workload. 2) Availability: 99.95% successful request rate (5xx and client-visible timeouts count as failures) measured per calendar month. 3) Error budget: 0.05% monthly budget; burn-rate rules apply per-window (see rollout gates). 4) Warm-start cache hit rate: target >= 60% for repeated prefixes for major enterprise tenants (for observability only).
rollout_gates: Gate A (internal beta): duration 72 hours, traffic routed to 100 internal accounts, no automated rollback; manual hold if p99 > 3x baseline or 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 30m. Gate B (canary public): 1% production traffic for 24 hours, automatic rollback if p99 increases by > 2.5x baseline AND 5xx rate > 0.2% for 15 minutes, or if error budget burn-rate > 4x over a 1h window. Gate C (staged ramp): progressive ramp 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days, pause if any of the following: sustained p95 > 1.5x baseline for 60m, availability below SLA target for 60m, or console-flagged customer-impact incidents. Each gate requires PM + Eng on-call ack for manual exceptions.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: runtime latency by model, region, and tenant; token-level cost and latency breakdowns; error budget panel. Alerts: - p99 latency increase by 100% vs baseline over 10m -> SEV-2; - 5xx rate > 0.2% sustained 15m -> SEV-1; - error budget burn-rate > 4x for 1h -> Pager to Reliability eng and PM. Alert runbooks must link to rollback playbook and PR/commit that triggered release. All queries to be written in PromQL and added to Console alert manager with explicit mute windows for planned tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SLOs documented in this ticket and merged into the SLO registry. 2) PromQL queries and Grafana/Console dashboards created and validated with synthetic traffic. 3) Alerting rules implemented with runbooks and verified by a simulated burn test. 4) Canary automation supports traffic split and automatic rollback based on the thresholds above. 5) PM review and sign-off on risk trade-offs and customer communication plan. 6) Post-rollout smoke test checklist added to release playbook.
implementation_notes: Engineering to implement metrics emission hooks where missing (token-level timing, per-tenant counters). Runtime team to add a canary routing flag and automated rollback lambda. Observability to coordinate PromQL and Console dashboard ownership. Use the dedicated canary tenant namespace and tag metrics with 'rollout_phase'. Document all changes in the release PR and link the PR to this ticket.
risks: 1) Noise in synthetic tests may mask real-world tail behaviors; mitigate by testing with production-like burst profiles. 2) Automatic rollback could cause flapping during intermittent infra issues; mitigate by combining multiple signals (latency AND error rate) before rollback. 3) Tenant-specific workloads might exceed error budget even if global SLOs are met; record high-impact tenants and plan targeted mitigations.
